newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-TWO WINS IN TWO DAYS FOR COMPAGNONI.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TWO WINS IN TWO DAYS FOR COMPAGNONI.

text.p: Italian world and Olympic champion Deborah Compagnoni clinched her second giant slalom victory in consecutive days in the women's Alpine skiing World Cup on Saturday.

After showing composure on a bumpy piste to win her first race of the season in the discipline on Friday, the 26-year-old Italian tamed an icy German piste again to hold off Austrian rival Anita Wachter for the second day running.

Compagnoni clinched her third World Cup victory of the season with an aggregate time of two minutes 8.37 seconds for the two runs, 0.90 seconds ahead of Wachter, who had held a slim lead after the first run.
Germany's Katja Seizinger, the overall World Cup champion who fell in Friday's race, bounced back to take third with 2:09.87.
The race proved to be another triumph for overall World Cup leader Pernilla Wiberg, who took fourth, just one hundreth of a second behind Seizinger, her main World Cup rival.
Wiberg, who had struggled with her giant slalom form before coming to the German races, still has a solid lead of 264 points over Seizinger in the overall rankings.
